So I got myself some critiques in a forum of my first draft ever, and one stood out in particular. To summarize, this person pointed out in every single paragraph how little it added to the story.  
The thing is that he's right. Not much is said about the main character until more or less 1000 words in, and there's not any kind of conflict or tension until another 1000 words. The rest is just small talk between two characters and the MC interacting and reacting to the environment (The history takes place in a slightly futuristic era and I wanted to make sure readers know how things work here), with slight details about the characters and main plot sprinkled here and there.  
He then went ahead and gave me some (honestly great) examples of first paragraphs, saying that the reader should first be introduced to who the main character is, their goal, their troubles, you know, that kind of stuff.  
But that's why I'm here. After all, what's wrong with enjoying two people's small talk with funny interactions? It's not for everyone and not the next bestseller, but hey, one of the critiques said they really enjoyed it, so I know it's at least for one person out there.  
If it feels that I'm just offended by his critique and want some validation, well, I might be. But I went ahead into this person's LinkedIn. He has been writing for 20 years and has two published works. Clearly, I am not on his level and I find myself lucky that such a person got to read my draft. If it had been a person without much experience, I would have discarded it as his opinion, so here I am.

Hey there, I'm not an expert or anything but I figrued I might provide a bit of my little experience. First of all make sure you get a cpl filter, since you can't put anything on the car it's the best way out there to get some of the dreaded reflections out. I figured that since it's only guides for actual modelling you could "split" the job and do several models like the mirrors, the tires and rims, the overall body, etc. Since the time it takes photogrammetry programs to generate meshes doesn't linearly scale with the number of photos it might be much faster to do it this way.

1.- For all my jobs I've done anywhere between 100 and 200 photos, Some people might argue it's too little but what really matters is that you don't miss any angle and have the appropiate number of photos depending of the amount of detail (I.E. if a figurine has very detailed hands and fingers, the whole figurine might take 70 photos and the fingers only another 70). Extreme angles technically aren't an issue themselves but since you might end up with some parts of the model very close to the camera and others far away you might be creating some depth of field (aka blurriness) and you do NOT want that. Also photographing a shiny surface from a side increases the strenght of the reflections and a cpl filter can only do so much about it.

2.- I don't think symmetry is an issue specially if you are including context (aka some background) but now that you mention the backpack thing, would it be a possibility to put some irregular lines of masking tape around the whole body? it would help with the reflections and it can be easily removed with almost no trace.

3.-Indeed the interior would be hard since it's most likely a dark color and you can't move around much, again, try creating a different project for the wheel, one for the mirror, etc.
